nm_scarry_wall.blurb: A small slab crag in the southern Box canyon complex outside Socorro, also known locally as Hidden Wall. It holds about 29 mostly bolted sport lines plus a few trad ones, with the bulk between 5.6 and 5.10 and only a couple of 5.11s and a very easy line or two. The rock is generally sound and the angle is friendly, which makes it a good place for someone stepping up to lead. The flat ground at the base is screened by brush, so it works for families and dogs, and the wall stays in shade until around midday. Check the top anchors carefully, since loose rock collects there.

nm_tiger_stripe_wall.blurb: The one sport wall in the Mesteno Canyon boulder zone near Roy, set on the slope facing the road-end parking across the drainage. It has 27 bolted routes with a few projects still open. Difficulty leans hard: most lines fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with a handful of 5.10s, a few 5.9s and one 5.8, and a single route above that. The sandstone here is brittle, so it is best treated gently and left alone when damp. Expect a quieter day than at the nearby boulders, with the wall split into a larger left side and a smaller right side.

nm_tram_the.blurb: A cluster of historic granite boulders in the Sandia foothills on the east edge of Albuquerque, right beside the tram terminal lot. The walk in is short. Across 27 problems the range is wide: a few V0 and V1 warm-ups, a good spread of V2 to V7, and a surprising number of hard lines from V8 up into the V10s. Rock quality is best nearest the trailhead, while some newer problems still shed flakes until they are cleaned. Plenty of unclimbed stone remains, so it suits both a quick session and someone wanting to explore.

nm_shady_side_2.blurb: The north-facing half of La Cueva in the Organ Mountains above Las Cruces, and the place to be when the desert turns hot. It carries 27 climbs, nearly all trad, with a few top-ropes and one boulder problem. Grades start with easy fifth-class ramps and chimneys, run through a solid middle band of 5.7 to 5.9, and top out in a couple of 5.11s. Lichen-covered slabs and crack systems are typical, and the face is described as reasonably solid. Reach it by trail from the picnic area; bring a standard trad rack.

nm_south_side_big_enchilada.blurb: The southwest-facing section of the Big Enchilada basalt cliff band at White Rock, near Los Alamos. It offers around 27 crack climbs, mostly trad with a handful of top-rope lines, and most need your own anchors. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 and 5.11. Ledges break up many of the lines, so they feel less sustained than at neighboring cliffs, and crowds are thin. The face catches sun from late morning onward, while the leftmost lines in an east-facing corner get earlier sun and more shade.

nm_todd_s_boulders.blurb: A sandstone bouldering spot on a small hill on the edge of Gallup, tucked between two hogbacks that give views and late-afternoon shade. Of its 27 problems, most sit between V0 and V4, with a good number of V3s, and a few tougher lines reaching V6 to V8; there is one VB. The best stone in the Gallup area is said to be here, though the zone is still being developed and some problems want a brushing first. The walk is brief, making it an easy stop on a day trip or while passing through town. Cell coverage is poor.

nm_rim_of_the_world_the.blurb: A southwest-facing granite crag high in Pecos Canyon northeast of Santa Fe, at roughly 8,800 feet, with views over the high peaks and few other parties. Of the 26 routes, nearly all are bolted sport lines and two are trad. Everything falls between 5.9 and 5.12, with most lines at 5.10 and 5.11 and a solid group of 5.12s, so it suits moderately strong climbers. The routes are among the longest in the canyon and of high quality. In summer the wall stays shaded until about mid-afternoon, then gets sun into the evening. The walk up is steep and takes a half hour or so.

nm_cattle_call_wall_area.blurb: The most visible cliff at Las Conchas in the Jemez Mountains, standing across a grassy meadow from the road at about 8,400 feet. It has 26 climbs, mostly sport with some trad and a few boulder problems. Grades are moderate: the bulk run 5.8 to 5.9, with a cluster of 5.11s and a couple of 5.12s, plus boulder problems from V2 to V5. That makes it a good fit for beginners and intermediates, and it is a popular instructional top-rope spot. It gets morning shade and afternoon sun, and summer weekends can bring big crowds.
nm_cattle_call_wall_area.parking_note: Use the roadside pullout on State Road 4 near the Las Conchas trailhead; the wall is in plain view across the meadow, only a very short walk away. The pullout fills up quickly because it is shared with hikers heading to the creek.
